## Background
On February 10-11, 13-17, and 15-20 2021, three successive severe winter storms hit Texas, resulting in a major power crisis. This analysis aims to visualize the impacts of these winter storms on homes in the Houston metropolitan area using remotely-sensed data on nighttime light intensity and OpenStreetMap data on buildings and roads.

## Load Packages and Source Functions
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(stars)
library(tmap)
library(here)
library(terra)
library(kableExtra)
```

## Import Data
```{r}
# Read in buildings data with query for homes
buildings <- sf::st_read(here::here(
   "data", "gis_osm_buildings_a_free_1.gpkg"), query = "SELECT *
FROM gis_osm_buildings_a_free_1
WHERE (type IS NULL AND name IS NULL)
OR type IN ('residential', 'apartments', 'house', 'static_caravan', 'detached')")

# Read in roads data with query for highways
roads <- sf::st_read(here::here(
   "data", "gis_osm_roads_free_1.gpkg"), query = "SELECT * FROM gis_osm_roads_free_1 WHERE fclass='motorway'")

# Read in lights data pre and post storm
lights_1_07 <- read_stars(here("data","VNP46A1", "VNP46A1.A2021038.h08v05.001.2021039064328.tif"))
lights_2_07 <- read_stars(here("data","VNP46A1", "VNP46A1.A2021038.h08v06.001.2021039064329.tif"))
lights_1_16 <- read_stars(here("data","VNP46A1","VNP46A1.A2021047.h08v05.001.2021048091106.tif"))
lights_2_16 <- read_stars(here("data","VNP46A1","VNP46A1.A2021047.h08v06.001.2021048091105.tif"))
```

```{r}
# Check that CRS of all data match
if(st_crs(buildings) == st_crs(roads) & st_crs(roads) == st_crs(lights_1_07) & st_crs(lights_1_07) == st_crs(lights_2_07) & st_crs(lights_2_07) == st_crs(lights_1_16) & st_crs(lights_1_16) == st_crs(lights_2_16)) {
  print("CRS MATCH")
}else{
  warning("CRS NOT A MATCH")
}

```

## Comparing Light Intensities Pre-Storm and Post-Storm

### Data Wrangling
```{r}
# Merge rasters for pre-storm and post-storm
lights_07 <- st_mosaic(lights_1_07, lights_2_07)
lights_16 <- st_mosaic(lights_1_16, lights_2_16)

# Create bounding box for Houston area
houston_bbox <- st_bbox(
  c(xmin = -96.5, ymin = 29, xmax = -94.5, ymax = 30.5),
  crs = st_crs(lights_07)
)

# Crop pre and post raster data to Houston
lights_07_houston <- st_crop(lights_07, houston_bbox)
lights_16_houston <- st_crop(lights_16, houston_bbox)

# Mask out unrealstic values from data
masked_houston_07 <-lights_07_houston
masked_houston_07[(masked_houston_07 > 1000) | (masked_houston_07 <= 0)] <- NA

masked_houston_16 <-lights_16_houston
masked_houston_16[(masked_houston_16 > 1000) | (masked_houston_16 <= 0)] <- NA
 
# Combine layers to one raster
combined_houston <- c(masked_houston_07, masked_houston_16)

# Rename layers
names(combined_houston) <- c(
  "February 7, 2021", "February 16, 2021"
)
```

### Map Light Intensities
```{r}
# Map the combined raster to show lights pre and post storm
tm_shape(combined_houston)+
  tm_raster(
    col.legend = tm_legend(
      title = "Light Intensity (nW cm^2 sr^1)",
      orientation = "landscape",
      title.size = 0.8,
      text.size = 0.8
    ),
    col.scale = tm_scale(values = "inferno")
  ) +
    tm_facets(ncol = 2, free.scales = FALSE) +
    tm_graticules(
      col = "white",
      lwd = 0.3,
      alpha = 0.2,
      labels.size = 0.5,
      labels.pos = c("left","bottom"),
      n.x = 4,
      n.y = 4
    ) +
      tm_layout(
        scale = 0.8,
        legend.position = tm_pos_out("center", "bottom"),
        legend.frame = TRUE,
        panels.labels = c(
          "February 7, 2021 (Pre-Storm)",
          "February 16, 2021 (Post-Storm)"
        ),
        panel.label.size = 1.0
      ) +
      tm_title("Nighttime Light Intensity in Houston Pre and Post 2021 Winter Storm")
```

From the maps produced, some areas have visibly lower light intensity in Houston after the storms, suggesting that blackouts may have occured.


## Create a Blackout Mask
Assuming that any location that experienced a drop of more than 200 nW cm^-2sr^-1 experienced a blackout, the raster data is reclassified to distinguish between locations that did or did not experience a blackout.
```{r}
# Calculate difference in light intensity between Feb 16 and Feb 7
light_dif <- rast(lights_07) - rast(lights_16)

# Create reclassification matrix using 200 threshold
rcl_lights <- matrix(c(-Inf, 200, NA,
                        200, Inf, 1),
                        ncol= 3, byrow =  TRUE)

# Reclassify lights matrix
reclass_lights <- classify(light_dif, rcl = rcl_lights)

# Vectorize reclassified raster
lights_vector <- st_as_stars(reclass_lights) |> 
  st_as_sf() |> 
  st_make_valid()

# Crop to Houston
houston_lights <- st_crop(lights_vector, houston_bbox)

# Reproject to Texas Centric Albers Equal Area CRS
houston_lights <- st_transform(houston_lights, crs = 3083)
```

## Exclude Highways From Blackout Mask
Highways may have experienced changes in their nighttime light intensities that are unrelated to the storms. Therefore, any locations within 200 meters of all highways in the Houston area are excluded from the analysis.
```{r}
# Ensure crs match 
roads <- st_transform(roads, crs = 3083)

# Create 200m buffer around highways
buffer_200m <- st_union(st_buffer(roads, dist=200))

# Exclude lights within buffer from data
non_hw_lights <- st_difference(houston_lights, buffer_200m)
```

## Identify homes in blackout areas

## Identify homes likely impacted by blackouts
```{r}
# Reproject to Texas Centric Albers Equal Area CRS
buildings <- st_transform(buildings, crs = 3083)

# Identify buildings in blackout areas
blackout_homes <- st_intersection(buildings, non_hw_lights)
```

```{r}
# Filter to homes in blackout areas
homes_blackout <- buildings |> 
  st_filter(non_hw_lights)

# Determine number of homes affected by blackout
n_homes_blackout <- nrow(homes_blackout)
```

From this analysis, it was determined that 157,410 houses were affected by the blackout following the 2021 winter storms in Houston. 

## Map Homes Affected by Blackouts

```{r}
# Create points for homes
homes_all <- st_centroid(buildings)
unaffected_homes <- homes_all[!homes_all$osm_id %in% blackout_homes$osm_id, ]
affected_homes <- st_centroid(blackout_homes)
```

```{r}
# Map affected and unaffected homes
tm_basemap("OpenStreetMap") + # Add basemap
  tm_shape(roads) +           # Map roads
  tm_lines(col = "darkgoldenrod1", lwd= 0.8) +
  tm_shape(unaffected_homes) +  # Map unaffected homes
  tm_dots(fill = "green", size = 0.01, fill_alpha = 0.3) +
  tm_shape(affected_homes) +  # Map affected homes
  tm_dots(fill = "red", size = 0.01, fill_alpha = 0.5) +
  tm_add_legend(
    type = "symbols",
    labels = c("Blackout", "No Blackout"),
    fill = c("red", "green"),
    shape = 21,
    size = 0.6,
    title = "Homes"
  ) +
  tm_title("Homes in Houston that Experienced Blackout after Feb 2021 Winter Storms") +
  tm_legend(
      type = "lines",
      labels = "Highways",
      col = "darkgoldenrod1",
      lwd = 0.8
    ) +
  tm_scalebar(position = c("right", "bottom"), text.size = 0.5) +
  tm_compass(position = c("right", "top"))
```

## Reflection
The map produced represents homes affected by the blackout after the February 2021 winter storms in red, and unaffected homes in green. Specifically, affected homes were defined as those that experienced a drop in light intensity greater than 200 nw cm^-2 sr^-1 following the winter storms, which was determined to be 157,410 homes from this analysis. This widespread loss of power is visible in the map, which shows vast areas of red indicating loss of power. The outages appear to be loosely clustered in the center, however homes in general are also clustered in the center. It should be acknowledged as well that this analysis has limitations. Due to cloud cover rendering some data unreliable, only two dates from before and after the storms are being compared. Using just these two dates as a proxy introduces some inaccuracy, as it operates under the assumption that these dates are representative. Further, increasing the raster resolution would allow for a more precise visual representation of affected and unaffected homes. Another limitation is that the 200 nw cm^-2 sr^-1 threshold may not actually capture all homes that experienced power outages following the storms. Further analysis may include other factors affecting power outages following the storms, such as socioeconomic factors, to determine whether impacts were disproportionately felt.
